case_analysis.thread_summary: AlpsAlpine 27BRD project thread (1792 lines). Covers full test execution lifecycle: RF PHY test (pass), RF test (pass), and profile tests for OPP and AVRCP (initial fail, root cause found, re-test pass). Three key technical/administrative findings: (1) A&W Bluetooth Stack 5.4 Host QDID combined with v5.2 Controller QDID generated 16 IDL Consistency Check errors due to spec version mismatch — resolved by switching to A&W v5.2 Host Stack QDID; (2) SIG Launchstudio login field changed from Username to Email Address; (3) Compliance Folder document list for End Product confirmed (operation manual, block diagram, outline drawing, antenna data sheet with radiation gain). Customer also requested early invoice issuance before work completion, which Allion accommodated.
all_questions_found: Why do we see 16 IDL errors when combining A&W Bluetooth Stack 5.4 QDID with a v5.2 Controller QDID?
How do we log in to SIG Launchstudio after the login field changed from username to email?
What documents are required for the Compliance Folder for an End Product?
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The IDL root cause is a Bluetooth specification version mismatch: the A&W 5.4 Host Stack ICS asserts features from v5.3/5.4 (extended advertising, ISO channels) that do not exist in the v5.2 Controller LL ICS, causing 16 Consistency Check IDL failures. The solution is to use the A&W Bluetooth Stack QDID whose version matches the Controller QDID (v5.2 in this case).
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: For any design combining a Host Stack QDID with a Controller QDID, the specification version of both QDIDs must match. If the Host Stack has multiple QDID versions available, always select the one that matches the Controller version to avoid IDL errors.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Version-mismatched QDID combinations generate IDL errors that block SIG registration approval. The 16 IDLs in this case would have caused submission rejection if not caught and fixed before registration.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: No direct mistake identified in the thread. Sakai caught and diagnosed the IDL issue proactively during the design review phase before registration was submitted.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always verify that Host Stack and Controller QDIDs share the same Bluetooth specification version before running the Consistency Check. A&W provides multiple QDID versions for their Host Stack — pick the version matching the customer's Controller QDID version. A quick version alignment check saves significant rework downstream.
